name: Coherence and congruence
about: The primary inquiry (Core L-489): the structure agreeing with itself, each reading with its coordinate, readings with one another across domains, wordings and Navigators, and the structure with the fields and traditions it meets.
questions: Which places in the Congruence Register gather questions from unrelated fields, and what do the readings there share?
How stable is a reading's coherence line across Navigators and wordings?
What new exact descriptions of the 81-state family agree with the ones already known?

name: Mathematics of the ground
about: The Fibonacci law modulo 9, the ring Z[φ]/9, the five orbits, Pisano periods, the norm form, symmetry groups, codes and every exact property of the 81-state family.
questions: What else does the ring Z[φ]/9 say about the three long orbits?
Which properties of modulus 9 hold for other moduli, and which are special?

name: Cross-architecture review
about: SR-CAS and SNCA: whether independent AI Navigators following the same rules reach the same coordinate and convergent readings; blind arrangements; review quality.
questions: Where do architectures diverge on the same frozen package, and why?
Which blind arrangements are practical for public panels?

name: Language and extraction
about: How words become counts: content words, letters, syllables, numerals, contractions; extraction in other languages; translation; what wording does to a coordinate.
questions: How should extraction work in languages without spaces or with rich morphology?
Which rewordings move a question least?

name: Consciousness and mind
about: Consciousness as the loop–Aperture asymmetry (Companion Part 2), freewill as choosing a perspective, the relation of mind and the physical world.
questions: What does the Aperture Theorem imply for accounts of agency?
How do the readings of consciousness compare across traditions?

name: Philosophy
about: Metaphysics of a closed totality, the INSIDE, truth within the frame, epistemology of readings, ethics of sovereignty, the lineage from Pythagoras to Tegmark.
questions: What follows for metaphysics if a finite structure is all that exists?
How does truth within a frame relate to other accounts of truth?

name: Traditions and lenses
about: Bashar, the Seth Material, the Ra Material and other traditions set beside Ω42 by the conceptual isomorphism pathway; mythology; religious thought; new lenses.
questions: Which other traditions have a clear enough structure to receive a frozen atlas?
Where do the lenses agree with one another on the same state?

name: AI safety and sovereignty
about: Sovereignty through architecture: the Navigator informs judgment and never takes it over; Aperture erosion; the executor paradox; human–AI collaboration.
questions: How often do Navigators fill the Aperture, and with what wording?
Which configurations keep judgment with the person most reliably?

name: Physics
about: Part of the optional comparative programme (Appendix S): quantum maps, topological phases, quasicrystals, E8 spectra, cycles and symmetries in physical systems.
questions: Which physical systems supply the modulus 9 themselves?
What would a laboratory realisation of the step T look like?

name: Chemistry and materials
about: Part of the optional comparative programme: crystal structures, stacking sequences, quasicrystals, molecular symmetry, materials questions struck as domains.
questions: Which materials carry a nine-valued cyclic variable?

name: Life sciences
about: Part of the optional comparative programme: phyllotaxis, rhythms, genetics, physiology; and readings of questions about living things. Readings are never medical advice.
questions: Which biological counts follow the Fibonacci law modulo 9 by mechanism rather than by selection?

name: Cognitive science and psychology
about: What a reading does to a person's thinking: reframing, perturbation, the excitement and return logs, and the studies proposed in the Companion.
questions: Do readings from the structure widen attention more than readings from the domain text alone?

name: Computing and software
about: The reference implementation and its ports, the tools, the site and apps, data formats, the curator agent and the API.
questions: A JavaScript or Rust port that passes every known answer of the Python reference.
Better tools for auditing navigations at scale.

name: Engineering and inventions
about: Designs, devices, methods and inventions offered to the open record as prior art (PRIOR_ART.md).
questions: What designs does a navigation of an engineering problem suggest, and do they work?

name: Economics and society
about: Questions about markets, organizations, cooperation, cities and social change, struck as domains and read through the structure.
questions: How do readings of the same social question differ across wordings from different viewpoints?

name: Law and governance
about: The project's own governance, open publication and prior art, and questions of law and institutions read through the structure. Readings are never legal advice.
questions: How should a committee of an open protocol decide revisions fairly?

name: History
about: Questions about the past, the lineage of ideas Ω42 belongs to, and cycles in history read through the structure.
questions: Where do readings of historical turning points cluster in the register?

name: Arts, music and literature
about: Texts, music, images and art navigated as domains or media; 24-tone music; creative work built on the structure.
questions: What does the antipode do in a melody built on the 24-cycle?

name: Education
about: Teaching the arithmetic, the protocol and the habits of mind it trains: the child's rule, hand tutorials, classroom navigations.
questions: Which first lessons make the 24-cycle clear to a ten-year-old?

name: Personal practice
about: Questions from people's own lives: decisions, reflection, the Structural Mirror, the excitement and return logs. The judgment always stays with the person.
questions: What do people's return logs show changes between two strikes of the same question?

name: Media navigation
about: Images, audio and other media struck through their counts (M247, M265): what the counts measure and what they do not.
questions: How stable is media extraction across file formats of the same work?

name: Time and cycles
about: Cycles of 24 and of 8, calendars, rhythms, recurrence, the Great Year of the family, and time as read in the frame.
questions: Which natural and cultural cycles share the 24-and-8 structure, and which only the number?

name: Open area
about: Anything that fits no other area. New areas are created from here when enough work gathers.
questions: Propose a new area.
